blocks.text:
If you missed crossing the equator during the night, the crew may issue their own equator-crossing certificate. Young explorers usually find this certificate especially exciting.

In the morning, you will land on the black-sand beaches of Puerto Egas in northwestern Santiago. A salt mine operated here in 1967. On a walk of around 2 hours, you can reach the abandoned mine, which now looks like a shallow saltwater lake.

Alternatively, stay near the beach, walk to the fur seal grottoes or go snorkelling to see sea turtles, sea lions and whitetip sharks.

Back on the yacht, lunch features flavours from South America's Pacific coast and Peruvian Nikkei-style dishes created by Pedro Miguel Schiaffino.

In the afternoon, boats will take you to Playa Espumilla. You will make a wet landing on a golden-sand beach known as a sea turtle breeding site. You will then visit Caleta Bucanero, where pirates rested and replenished their supplies of fresh water and turtle meat in the 17th century.

You can end the day with snorkelling, kayaking or canoeing. Back on board, you will be welcomed with a Bloody Mary cocktail before the yacht sails to the next stop on the programme.
